cells.tense: What has been growing under patient care is ready now and is being met on time.
cells.act: release the method, not the purpose
cells.ask: Drop the one piece of your care that has become reflex rather than need. Keep the commitment underneath it. No deadline — just notice what the week does without that piece.
cells.core:
You can bring something to its finish and then open your hands. What you have built is holding itself up, and you are letting it, piece by piece. The room is big, the light is steady, and the hand does not have to stay on it to keep it safe. The long work shows, and you get to stand in this part of it.

One part of the care you are still doing is reflex now rather than need. Set that part down and leave the purpose untouched. What you are committed to stays visible without it. Old hands will reach for the missing piece and find it gone. That is how you find out which part was the commitment and which part was only a method.
cells.sheetLine: You can finish, open your hands, and like what grew.
cells.verb: bring a long-tended thing to its finish
cells.place: where the pattern gets set for what comes next

cells.tense: The result will be ripe and the work will be kept hovering over it long past that point.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Do one real piece of the work alongside someone else. Not a hand-off and not a report — the same job, same day, so their way of doing it changes yours. No timeline.
cells.core:
Where the growing has come in, it is being held too tight. Each result is still being improved on, and the next version is being planned while this one is still coming up. It looks like devotion from outside. From the bed it reads as a thing that cannot be done. You know how to care for something. What is missing is trusting that someone else's care can hold it too.

Bring one person into the work and do it side by side, same job, same room, their way of doing it bending the shape of yours. What has already grown stays yours when you look at it again. You do not have to be the only hands it passes through to keep it safe.
cells.sheetLine: You are improving what is ready instead of letting it be done.

cells.tense: The place where the pattern gets set has sat unused since the last person who set it there left.
cells.act: face one way for three days
cells.ask: Pick one direction for your own growing by what you want, not what makes sense, and hold it for three days. Stop checking the other directions before you have moved.
cells.core:
The room where the pattern gets set has gone quiet, and nothing new has been started in it for a while. You tend what is already there, but the arranging hand has slipped off the table. What you built earlier is holding; you have stopped adding to it and stopped saying where it should go next.

Choose a heading. Not the correct one — the wanted one. Hold it for three days and take the small decisions about the growing in that direction, and stop checking the other directions before you have moved. The point is not picking the right one. The point is finding out whether your hand still answers when you use it, and what it reaches for first.

cells.tense: The structure is being set and the hand doing the setting is calling it the season's doing.
cells.act: drop the wrong approach and keep the commitment
cells.ask: Next time your patience turns out to be a choice, let that be true without explaining it away. Notice the choice — nothing else about the week changes.
cells.core:
The shape of the thing is being decided by you — the timing, the order, when to hold off and when to move — and your account of it is that this is simply how things come in. The pattern is real and it belongs to you. You have filed it under the garden's own nature. The garden does not mind. The people watching learn from a hand they cannot see, and that hand is doing more than it lets on.

The next time you make a call about your growing, let yourself know it was a call you made. Nothing else changes — same work, same pace, same answers. The pen is down on paper you were already writing. The words on the page stay the same.
cells.sheetLine: The pattern is yours and you filed it under the garden's own nature.
